One might be tempted by the word "Renegotiation", which suggests dealings with contractors, but it appears only in the proper name of an Act and account title. The section establishes no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.

opus.w: This section only adds $4,000,000 to an existing appropriation account. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The word "Renegotiation" appears only in the name of the account and does not involve any outside party in a decision.
opus.s: For an additional amount for “Refunds under Renegotiation Act, 1950”, $4,000,000.
opus.b:
1. **Analysis:** The word "Renegotiation" might suggest bargaining between the government and outside parties. That reading fails. The phrase "Refunds under Renegotiation Act, 1950" just names the budget account receiving the money. The section only provides an extra $4,000,000 to that account. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in a federal decision.
